target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech labs doing mass spectrometry for biologics and cell and gene therapy development
problem: Sample preparation for mass spectrometry is slow and technically difficult, and hard-to-detect chemicals used in drug manufacturing are hard to measure. Andson sells a microfluidic chip system to speed this up.
business_model: Hardware instrument plus consumable chips sold to labs
product_category: Life science tools, microfluidic sample preparation

founders.name: Mason Chilmonczyk
founders.background_notes: Trained as a mechanical engineer; DynaChip was invented during his Ph.D.

founders.name: Andrei Fedorov
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Hypepotamus and Georgia Tech; not listed on the YC page.

investors: Unnamed lead investor from the biotech industry

technical_complexity.rationale: Microfabricated chips plus instrument integration with mass spectrometers requires hardware, microfluidics and analytical chemistry expertise from a university spinout.

defensibility.rationale: University-derived IP and trademarked DynaChip product plus lab workflow lock-in; patent status was not verified.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found through 2025.

market_need_then: Cell and gene therapy and biologics developers needed faster analytics; the company was launched through Georgia Tech with the NSF Engineering Research Center for Cell Manufacturing Technologies.

branding.domain_note: Uses andsonbiotech.com, a descriptive suffix domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, mission style: remove technical barriers to ambitious discoveries

brand_strength.rationale: Only trade and university press coverage found; the product brand DynaChip matters more than the company name in a B2B niche.

outcome_analysis: Andson spun out of Georgia Tech research and raised a $3.6M seed in April 2024 and a further $5M reported in October 2025, later than most YC peers, which fits slow hardware sales cycles. It is active with 12 listed staff on YC. The commercial scale is not public.
notes: Competitors list is empty: a dated search found no source from 2021 to 2022 naming rivals; 908 Devices ZipChip appeared only in an undated Thermo Fisher blog. Conflicts: Preqin lists a $4.7M seed and total, an Instrument Business Outlook snippet names Glenn H. Epstein as seed lead (not opened); investors left empty. The 2025 round stage is not stated by Hypepotamus so recorded as other.
